raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Adaptive speculative decoding currently routes by batch size. Controlled H100 measurements show that logical sequence length is an additional useful routing signal, but not because deeper drafting universally wins at long context.

At fixed BS=8, two counterbalanced server-order passes (three measured batches per pass after warmup) produced:

| Logical context | Winning K | Margin over runner-up |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 | 7 | 15.48% |
| 1,024 | 7 | 20.43% |
| 4,096 | 7 | 2.14% |
| 8,192 | 1 | 1.97% |
| 16,384 | 1 | 4.56% |

All output hashes matched, and end-to-end wall throughput showed the same K=7 to K=1 transition. In this workload, draft acceptance stayed high through context 4,096, then fell to roughly 1.5--1.6 at 8,192 and roughly 1.004 at 16,384, making deeper drafting overhead at long context. This is evidence for exposing context as a policy input, not for a universal context-to-K default. Full setup and limitations are recorded in [the roadmap evidence update](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/23705#issuecomment-6023973196).

## Relationship to current adaptive-spec work

PR #37274 / commit `83bd2c473f` added injected `AdaptiveSpecPolicy` support after this PR was first opened. This rebase treats that as the current ownership boundary:

- The existing batch-only `AdaptiveSpecPolicy` interface remains unchanged, so third-party/custom policies written for #37274 continue to work.
- This PR adds a separately detected, optional `ContextAwareAdaptiveSpecPolicy` capability.
- `AdaptiveSpeculativeParams` implements that capability using independent `(batch size, context bucket)` slots; it does not replace the controller or throughput-aware policy work.
- The default 1D configuration and its behavior remain unchanged.

The non-overlapping contribution here is therefore the context signal, optional 2D slot schema, runtime-state reachability union, and end-to-end wiring.

## Changes

### Optional 2D configuration

Each per-BS entry may contain `ctx_buckets`:

```json
{
  "8": {
    "ctx_buckets": {
      "1-2047": {"candidate_steps": [0, 1, 3]},
      "2048-32768": {"candidate_steps": [1, 3]}
    }
  }
}
```

- Ranges are 1-indexed, inclusive, and must start at 1 with no gaps.
- A context above the configured final upper bound uses the final bucket.
- Entries without `ctx_buckets` retain the legacy single-slot behavior.
- Candidate steps are unioned across every context bucket when runtime states are built and CUDA-graph batch sizes are pruned. Graph capture remains BS-only; no context dimension is added to the capture set.

### CPU-only routing signal

`get_batch_context_length()` takes the upper median of `Req.seqlen` across the batch. `Req.seqlen` is already CPU-resident Python state, so routing adds no device-to-host synchronization in the decode hot path.

The signal is threaded through:

- EAGLE and frozen-KV MTP activation before drafting;
- scheduler-side acceptance feedback after accepted lengths are available on CPU;
- `BaseSpecWorker`, EAGLE, and NGRAM hook signatures; and
- the plain `BaseTpWorker` mirror used by non-last pipeline-parallel stages.

## Compatibility properties

- Legacy JSON configs route exactly as before.
- Legacy custom policies receive only the original batch-only calls even when the controller is given `ctx_repr`.
- Context-aware policies opt in structurally through two separate methods.
- The CUDA-graph capture set for a 2D config is identical to the corresponding 1D config whose per-BS candidates are the union of all context buckets.

## Validation

- Repository `pre-commit` hooks pass on all 10 changed files, including AST, isort, Ruff, Ruff format, codespell, and registered-test validation.
- `compileall` passes on all changed Python files.
- 55 unit tests pass in a direct real-module harness, covering the existing adaptive tests plus:
  - schema validation and context-boundary routing;
  - isolated EMA state per context bucket;
  - candidate and CUDA-graph reachability unions;
  - capture-set identity versus the equivalent 1D union;
  - unchanged dispatch for an injected legacy custom policy;
  - opt-in context-policy dispatch; and
  - empty-batch and upper-median context statistics.

The normal local pytest import path is unavailable on the current macOS development host because the SGLang runtime dependencies (`pybase64`, then Triton) are not installed. CI remains the authoritative full-environment run.

### Prior live-server routing smoke

Before this latest-main rebase, the same 2D routing path was exercised on an H100 NVL with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct plus the SGLang EAGLE3 draft:

| Case | BS | Prompt length | Configured route | Observed `sglang:spec_num_steps` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| short | 1 | ~10 | K=3 | 3.0 |
| short | 8 | ~3 | K=0 | 0.0 |
| longer | 8 | 262 | K=3 | 3.0 |

This confirms end-to-end context-slot selection, but it is historical smoke evidence rather than a fresh performance validation of the rebased commit.

## References

- #37274 — injected adaptive policy/controller interface integrated by this rebase
- #23705 — roadmap and controlled H100 evidence
- vLLM RFC #48627 / PR #48944 — related context-aware speculative-routing work

Hi maintainers — this is an external contributor PR, so the `pr-gate` check is blocked on the `run-ci` label per the [contribution guide](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests). Could someone with triage permission add the `run-ci` label so CI can run?

Quick summary of what's in the PR:
- Extends the existing adaptive spec `_route` from BS-only to BS × ctx (2D config schema; legacy 1D configs stay inert).
- All ctx_repr computation is CPU-side (from `batch.reqs`), no host-device sync in the decode hot path.
- 46/46 unit tests pass locally; live-server smoke on H100 NVL confirms 3-case routing (details in PR body).
- Sibling implementation: vLLM RFC #48627 / PR #48944.

Happy to address any changes needed once CI signals. Thanks!

Hi @Qiaolin-Yu @alphabetc1 — could I get a quick direction check on this PR?

The narrow question is whether extending adaptive speculative routing from BS-only to **BS × logical context length** is still a direction you would consider upstreaming. A simple **yes / no (or park for now)** would be very helpful before I invest further in the implementation.

I am rebasing the existing patch onto current `main` to clear the stale-base CI gate, but I will keep the scope unchanged and avoid further expansion until there is maintainer direction. If the preferred architecture has changed, I am also happy to adapt or close this cleanly.

Thank you for taking a look.

An evidence update before rebasing this old implementation: the new controlled H100 screen supports logical context as a useful routing axis, but it does **not** support the mechanism claim currently stated in this PR body.

At fixed BS=8, two counterbalanced server-order passes (three measured batches per pass after warmup) produced these static-step winners:

| logical context | winning K | margin over runner-up |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 | 7 | 15.48% |
| 1024 | 7 | 20.43% |
| 4096 | 7 | 2.14% |
| 8192 | 1 | 1.97% |
| 16384 | 1 | 4.56% |

All output hashes matched. End-to-end wall throughput showed the same K=7 to K=1 transition. In this workload, the latest SpecForge draft kept high acceptance through context 4096, then acceptance length fell to roughly 1.5--1.6 at 8192 and roughly 1.004 at 16384. Deeper drafting therefore became overhead at long context; this is the opposite of the original KV-amortization-only motivation in the PR body.

Full setup, limitations, and pooled numbers are recorded in the roadmap thread: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/23705#issuecomment-6023973196. In particular, this is one H100, one target/draft pair, BS=8, and a draft whose model card requires the longer-context override. It is evidence for a context hook, not a universal default policy.

Given the newer AdaptiveStepRouter/controller structure, would you prefer that I:

1. rebase this as a narrow logical-context input/slot extension to the current shared router, with the motivation and tests rewritten around the measured evidence; or
2. close #31716 because the current throughput-aware controller supersedes a static context axis?

I will hold the large rebase until there is a direction signal, so the implementation does not churn against a policy the project no longer wants.

I went ahead with the latest-`main` rebase and compatibility work so this can now be reviewed as a concrete, current patch rather than as a direction question.

Overlap classification:

- #37274 owns the injected batch-only `AdaptiveSpecPolicy` / controller abstraction.
- This PR now preserves that interface exactly and adds context support as a separately detected optional capability, so existing custom policies do not receive new positional/keyword arguments.
- The remaining scope is non-overlapping: the CPU-only context statistic, optional `(BS, ctx)` slots, candidate/CUDA-graph reachability union, EAGLE + frozen-KV MTP routing, scheduler feedback, and the pipeline-parallel mirror hook.

The branch is rebased onto upstream `main` at `961bcf481d`; the new single commit is `459040a390`. I also rewrote the motivation to match the H100 evidence: context is useful because the winning K changed from 7 to 1 as acceptance collapsed at long context in this workload, not because higher K universally wins at long context.

Local validation on the rebased diff:

- all repository pre-commit hooks for the 10 changed files pass;
- `compileall` passes;
- 55 adaptive-policy/routing unit tests pass through a direct real-module harness, including legacy injected-policy compatibility and opt-in context-policy dispatch.

The PR body now documents the exact ownership boundary, evidence limitations, and the fact that the prior H100 live-server smoke predates this rebase. Full CI still needs the normal maintainer-triggered gate.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a 2D routing schema for adaptive speculative decoding, allowing step selection to be parameterized by both batch size and a context length representation (ctx_repr). It updates the speculative workers and managers to compute and propagate this context representation and adds extensive unit tests for validation and routing. The review feedback highlights a critical performance issue where calculating the median sequence length using PyTorch tensors on the GPU (or via .item()) causes synchronous GPU-to-CPU transfers in the hot path. The reviewer suggests computing the median directly on the CPU using the sequence lengths available in batch.reqs to avoid this overhead.

Using `batch.seq_lens.median().item()` or `batch.seq_lens_cpu.median().item()` introduces a synchronous GPU-to-CPU transfer (`.item()`) or unnecessary PyTorch tensor overhead in the hot path of decode iterations. Under CUDA graphs, `batch.seq_lens_cpu` is `None`, which forces a synchronous GPU-to-CPU transfer on every single decode step, severely degrading performance and causing CPU-GPU bubbles.

Since `batch.reqs` is already on the CPU and contains the exact same sequence length information via `req.seqlen`, we can compute the median directly on the CPU using a simple sorted list indexing. This completely avoids any host-device synchronization and PyTorch tensor overhead.

Correct catch — this exact sync bubble is what vLLM RFC #48627 (sibling proposal) called out as an anti-pattern, and my initial elif seq_lens.median().item() fallback silently re-introduced it. +            params.on_verify_complete_for_context([3, 3, 3], batch_size=8, ctx_repr=500)
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(low_slot.ema_accept_len, 1.0)
+        self.assertEqual(high_slot.ema_accept_len, untouched_ema)
+
+    def test_cuda_graph_bs_for_step_uses_union_of_2d_buckets(self):
+        params = self._params()
+        params.set_cuda_graph_bs([4, 8, 16, 32])
+        self.assertEqual(params.cuda_graph_bs_for_step(3), [4, 8, 16, 32])
+
+    def test_capture_set_identical_to_1d_union(self):
+        # "capture set stays BS-only": for any 2D config, cuda_graph_bs_for_step
+        # returns the same list as the 1D config whose candidate_steps at each
+        # BS is the union of that BS's 2D bucket palettes. Proves no new K
+        # regime is introduced by the ctx axis.
+        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False) as f:
+            json.dump(
+                {
+                    "1": {"candidate_steps": [1, 3, 7]},
+                    "8": {
+                        "ctx_buckets": {
+                            "1-2047": {"candidate_steps": [0, 1, 3]},
+                            "2048-32768": {"candidate_steps": [1, 3]},
+                        },
+                    },
+                    "32": {
+                        "ctx_buckets": {
+                            "1-767": {"candidate_steps": [0]},
+                            "768-32768": {"candidate_steps": [1, 3]},
+                        },
+                    },
+                    "64": {"candidate_steps": [0]},
+                },
+                f,
+            )
+            f.flush()
+            params_2d = AdaptiveSpeculativeParams(initial_steps=3, cfg_path=f.name)
+        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False) as f:
+            json.dump(
+                {
+                    "1": {"candidate_steps": [1, 3, 7]},
+                    "8": {"candidate_steps": [0, 1, 3]},
+                    "32": {"candidate_steps": [0, 1, 3]},
+                    "64": {"candidate_steps": [0]},
+                },
+                f,
+            )
+            f.flush()
+            params_1d = AdaptiveSpeculativeParams(initial_steps=3, cfg_path=f.name)
+        params_2d.set_cuda_graph_bs([4, 8, 16, 32])
+        params_1d.set_cuda_graph_bs([4, 8, 16, 32])
+        for step in (0, 1, 3, 7):
+            self.assertEqual(
+                params_2d.cuda_graph_bs_for_step(step),
+                params_1d.cuda_graph_bs_for_step(step),
+            )
+        self.assertEqual(params_2d.candidate_steps, params_1d.candidate_steps)

Using `batch.seq_lens.median().item()` or `batch.seq_lens_cpu.median().item()` introduces a synchronous GPU-to-CPU transfer (`.item()`) or unnecessary PyTorch tensor overhead in the hot path of decode iterations. Under CUDA graphs, `batch.seq_lens_cpu` is `None`, which forces a synchronous GPU-to-CPU transfer on every single decode step, severely degrading performance and causing CPU-GPU bubbles.

Since `batch.reqs` is already on the CPU and contains the exact same sequence length information via `req.seqlen`, we can compute the median directly on the CPU using a simple sorted list indexing. This completely avoids any host-device synchronization and PyTorch tensor overhead.

```suggestion
        if batch.reqs:
            seqlens = sorted(req.seqlen for req in batch.reqs)
            ctx_repr = seqlens[len(seqlens) // 2]
        else:
            ctx_repr = 0
```

Correct catch — this exact sync bubble is what vLLM RFC #48627 (sibling proposal) called out as an anti-pattern, and my initial elif seq_lens.median().item() fallback silently re-introduced it. Fixed in 7d2825af: ctx_repr is now computed from sorted(req.seqlen for req in batch.reqs)[n//2] — Req.seqlen is a pure-Python property (len(origin_input_ids) + len(output_ids)) equivalent to seq_lens_cpu[i] in physical meaning, with no tensor allocation and no host-device sync. Hi maintainers — this is an external contributor PR, so the `pr-gate` check is blocked on the `run-ci` label per the [contribution guide](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests). Could someone with triage permission add the `run-ci` label so CI can run?

Quick summary of what's in the PR:
- Extends the existing adaptive spec `_route` from BS-only to BS × ctx (2D config schema; legacy 1D configs stay inert).
- All ctx_repr computation is CPU-side (from `batch.reqs`), no host-device sync in the decode hot path.
- 46/46 unit tests pass locally; live-server smoke on H100 NVL confirms 3-case routing (details in PR body).
- Sibling implementation: vLLM RFC #48627 / PR #48944.

Happy to address any changes needed once CI signals. Thanks!

Hi @Qiaolin-Yu @alphabetc1 — could I get a quick direction check on this PR?

The narrow question is whether extending adaptive speculative routing from BS-only to **BS × logical context length** is still a direction you would consider upstreaming. A simple **yes / no (or park for now)** would be very helpful before I invest further in the implementation.

I am rebasing the existing patch onto current `main` to clear the stale-base CI gate, but I will keep the scope unchanged and avoid further expansion until there is maintainer direction. If the preferred architecture has changed, I am also happy to adapt or close this cleanly.

Thank you for taking a look.

An evidence update before rebasing this old implementation: the new controlled H100 screen supports logical context as a useful routing axis, but it does **not** support the mechanism claim currently stated in this PR body.

At fixed BS=8, two counterbalanced server-order passes (three measured batches per pass after warmup) produced these static-step winners:

| logical context | winning K | margin over runner-up |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 | 7 | 15.48% |
| 1024 | 7 | 20.43% |
| 4096 | 7 | 2.14% |
| 8192 | 1 | 1.97% |
| 16384 | 1 | 4.56% |

All output hashes matched. End-to-end wall throughput showed the same K=7 to K=1 transition. In this workload, the latest SpecForge draft kept high acceptance through context 4096, then acceptance length fell to roughly 1.5--1.6 at 8192 and roughly 1.004 at 16384. Deeper drafting therefore became overhead at long context; this is the opposite of the original KV-amortization-only motivation in the PR body.

Full setup, limitations, and pooled numbers are recorded in the roadmap thread: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/23705#issuecomment-6023973196. In particular, this is one H100, one target/draft pair, BS=8, and a draft whose model card requires the longer-context override. It is evidence for a context hook, not a universal default policy.

Given the newer AdaptiveStepRouter/controller structure, would you prefer that I:

1. rebase this as a narrow logical-context input/slot extension to the current shared router, with the motivation and tests rewritten around the measured evidence; or
2. close #31716 because the current throughput-aware controller supersedes a static context axis?

I will hold the large rebase until there is a direction signal, so the implementation does not churn against a policy the project no longer wants.

I went ahead with the latest-`main` rebase and compatibility work so this can now be reviewed as a concrete, current patch rather than as a direction question.

Overlap classification:

- #37274 owns the injected batch-only `AdaptiveSpecPolicy` / controller abstraction.
- This PR now preserves that interface exactly and adds context support as a separately detected optional capability, so existing custom policies do not receive new positional/keyword arguments.
- The remaining scope is non-overlapping: the CPU-only context statistic, optional `(BS, ctx)` slots, candidate/CUDA-graph reachability union, EAGLE + frozen-KV MTP routing, scheduler feedback, and the pipeline-parallel mirror hook.

The branch is rebased onto upstream `main` at `961bcf481d`; the new single commit is `459040a390`. I also rewrote the motivation to match the H100 evidence: context is useful because the winning K changed from 7 to 1 as acceptance collapsed at long context in this workload, not because higher K universally wins at long context.

Local validation on the rebased diff:

- all repository pre-commit hooks for the 10 changed files pass;
- `compileall` passes;
- 55 adaptive-policy/routing unit tests pass through a direct real-module harness, including legacy injected-policy compatibility and opt-in context-policy dispatch.

The PR body now documents the exact ownership boundary, evidence limitations, and the fact that the prior H100 live-server smoke predates this rebase. Full CI still needs the normal maintainer-triggered gate.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a 2D routing schema for adaptive speculative decoding, allowing step selection to be parameterized by both batch size and a context length representation (ctx_repr). It updates the speculative workers and managers to compute and propagate this context representation and adds extensive unit tests for validation and routing. The review feedback highlights a critical performance issue where calculating the median sequence length using PyTorch tensors on the GPU (or via .item()) causes synchronous GPU-to-CPU transfers in the hot path. The reviewer suggests computing the median directly on the CPU using the sequence lengths available in batch.reqs to avoid this overhead.
